headline: Bitcoin sinks 6.6 percent to 63,755 dollars as weekend crypto rout deepens on Fed hike bets
subhead: Ether fell 9.2 percent to 1,750.7 and bitcoin sits 34.2 percent below its 52-week high, while the S&P 500 closed Friday down 0.4 percent at 7,561.7 ahead of Nvidia results on Tuesday.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 0.4 percent to 7,561.7 and the Nasdaq 0.9 percent to 25,136.3 as AMD dropped 8.8 percent and Broadcom 4.8 percent on profit-taking.
October PPI rose 0.3 percent for 6.5 percent annual wholesale inflation; the 10-year yield rose to 5.15 percent with a December Fed hike fully priced.
Week ahead: Nvidia reports Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, and Anthropic is expected to price Wednesday at 70 to 78 dollars a share.

india.text: Nifty fell 0.6 percent to 25,144.3 and Bank Nifty 0.8 percent to 61,034.1 on 13 November as October CPI hit 6.09 percent and Brent neared 96 dollars.
FIIs net bought about Rs 5,736.6 crore in cash on 13 November while DIIs net sold about Rs 2,254 crore, extending a foreign buying streak.
Rupee weakened 21 paise to 94.24 per dollar on 13 November as higher crude prices and US Treasury yields added pressure.

global.text: Asia on 13 November: Nikkei closed at 61,142.35, while the Hang Seng fell to 23,637.60 and Kospi to 5,290.53 as chip worries lingered.
Europe: the FTSE 100 closed at a three-month high of 10,902.56 on insurers, energy and consumer stocks, while the DAX slipped.
Bitcoin fell 6.6 percent to about 63,755 dollars over the weekend and ether 9.2 percent, with about 1 billion dollars liquidated on Fed hike bets.

weekly.narrative: Jensen Huang's sudden exit as Nvidia CEO dominated the week: Nvidia fell 12.8 percent, but rotation into Apple, AMD and Broadcom still left the S&P 500 up 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq up 2.3 percent despite a Friday AI selloff. Hot US CPI and 6.5 percent annual PPI pushed the 10-year yield to 5.15 percent and left a December Fed hike fully priced, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high. That weighed on metals and crypto: gold fell 4.6 percent to a 13-month low, silver 5.4 percent and bitcoin broke below 70,000 dollars. India leaned on nine straight sessions of foreign buying and a bank rally, though the Nifty slipped to 25,144.3 on Friday after October CPI rose to 6.09 percent. Next week brings Nvidia results on 17 November, FOMC minutes on 18 November and Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut on 19 November.
